reason: Correct an actual replay bug: profession-specific Yes/No questions were misclassified as activity checkboxes because their options contain career IDs. Dispatch by question kind first. Replace the arbitrary three-comparison cap with uniform coverage of all mapped subject-aligned professions. Shared activity questions are answered once. No changes to profiles, answer bindings, numeric scoring, Top support gates, or education/salary ranking.
limitations: Bindings are authored test assumptions, not learned weights or independent validation.

Unmapped or unstated specialist preferences remain unfamiliar; unknown official 60-item responses use neutral 3 and are explicitly marked as simulation conventions. Positive official responses use Like (4), negative responses Dislike (2), with no invented intensity.
Option answers are simulated only when every linked career has an authored binding and its shared constructs are known.
Original 172 profiles retain their existing structured answers and provenance; original data is not rewritten.

200 additional holdouts were assigned before outcome runs and receive no case-specific edits. Earlier aggregate results have been seen, so this is not an untouched final validation set. Original 30 and fresh 12 holdouts remain separately identified.
Historical failed policies are preserved in research only; no historical word classifier is imported in the release pipeline.

developmentDiagnostic.scope: Development-only diagnostic before this policy freeze; not a released result. Holdout cases not inspected or customized.
developmentDiagnostic.degreeMetricNote: The diagnostic degree count includes any supported degree career. The chart retains the first-three Top cap and separately reports supported degree options outside that cap.

exposureProtocol: All mapped careers whose required subject constructs are explicitly positive receive their available questions; no salary, degree, match quota or successful-outcome stopping. This is comprehensive questionnaire coverage, not typical student behavior.
